question: Manjit has borrowed an amount of ₹2,20,000 from a bank to start a business. How much simple interest (in ₹) will he pay at a rate of 4% per annum after 2 years?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net **interest percentage** for 2 years = Rate × Time = 4% × 2 = 8%

Simple Interest = 8% of ₹2,20,000

Simple Interest = 0.08 × 2,20,000 = ₹17,600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹17,600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹2,20,000

Rate (R) = 4% per annum

Time (T) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/006bffda5e24faa6acf8788b4c118ef6d89b46d1d5d7f2fa23b2dd0fbd440b46.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = (2,20,000 × 4 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 2,200 × 8

⇒ SI = ₹17,600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹17,600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount Formula

The total amount (A) to be paid back is the sum of Principal and Simple Interest: A = P + SI.

Rate of Interest Calculation

To find the rate when SI, P, and T are known: R = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T).

SI vs CI for 2 Years

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for 2 years is: CI − SI = P(R/100)².
